Routing policies: hosted vs dedicated vs private
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time - I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Samir our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Laura Gomez: Hi Maya, hi Samir, Laura here. We invited Ethan and Priya to cover ML + security. Marco might drop in.
[00:12] Samir Patel: Great, thanks. We'll do a quick slide + live console demo - focus on per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown since you told us that's top of mind.
[00:20] Ethan Ruiz: Yep, cost is huge for the inference workloads, and latency is non-negotiable for some flows.
[00:26] Priya Nair: And we need clarity on data residency, KMS, audit logs. We'll flag any red flags early.
[00:31] Maya Chen: Totally. Quick agenda: 1) usage analytics overview 2) per-route dashboards 3) cost breakdown + examples 4) next steps + pilot.
[00:40] Samir Patel: Starting in the console now - apologies if the screen share is a bit laggy. So here's the global usage view, token volumes by day, and a heatmap by route. Notice you can group by model, route, and tag.
[00:56] Samir Patel: You mentioned you have high-volume triage chat routes and low-volume report generation routes. The per-route dashboard surfaces top consumers, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k requests, and tail latency.
[01:14] Laura Gomez: Can you show an example of cost per route? We currently estimate cost in-house and it's messy.
[01:19] Samir Patel: Sure. Switch to the 'Cost Insights' tab - here's an example for a retail customer but same mechanics. Each route shows breakdown: model time (GPU), token count, prefix cache hit rate, and any batching savings. You can drill into a date range and see a simulated cost if you switch model variants or enable quantization.
[01:36] Ethan Ruiz: That simulated cost model - how accurate is it? We need it to map to actual spend in a pilot.
[01:42] Samir Patel: Good question. The simulation uses measured per-token latency profiles and our kernel-cost table for the selected hardware. For hosted customers it's within ~10-15% historically; for Dedicated we can calibrate with a short benchmark run.
[01:56] Priya Nair: Hosted means data leaves our VPC, right? We need VPC or private.
[02:01] Maya Chen: For PII/regulatory folks, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem. You'll still get the same console UI, it's just the control plane is private. We can include KMS integration and audit logs.
[02:13] Laura Gomez: Good. For the per-route views - can we set alerts on cost thresholds? We run a few bursty routes and want automatic alerts if cost or tail latency spikes.
[02:21] Samir Patel: Yes - alerts, rate-limit policies, and automatic fallback rules. You can set a per-route alert for cost per hour or p95 latency; when breached you can route to a cheaper model variant or into a degraded mode.
[02:35] Marco (PM): Sorry jumping in - what's the difference between quantization savings vs caching savings?
[02:40] Samir Patel: Quantization reduces model execution cost by using lower-precision kernels; savings depend on model and accuracy tolerance. Caching (prefix/KV cache) reduces tokens processed - for chat flows we often see big wins because of repeated prefixes. Our console shows cache hit-rate and estimated token savings.
[02:55] Ethan Ruiz: Our triage chat has a lot of repeated prompts, so caching could be big. We also use a hub model with multiple route variants.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Right - the per-route dashboard will show top templates and prefix reuse; you can build a rule that stores top N prefixes in the KV cache automatically.
[03:10] Laura Gomez: Any examples of customers who've cut cost 30-40%?
[03:14] Maya Chen: Yes, we ran an Optimize engagement with a fintech customer - combinational caching and switching to a quantized variant during non-peak hours gave them ~35% unit-cost reduction without noticeable quality regression.
[03:24] Priya Nair: About logs - what do audit logs contain? Do they include full prompts?
[03:30] Samir Patel: Audit logs capture request metadata by default: route, model version, latencies, token counts, user id (if provided). You can opt in to store full payloads, but we advise masking PII. For Private deployments, logs stay in your VPC; for Hosted we offer retention controls and certs.
[03:45] Ethan Ruiz: For Hosted, is KMS customer-managed?
[03:48] Maya Chen: We support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest via KMS integrations; for Private deployments you can bring your own HSM.
[03:55] Laura Gomez: Ok. Can you walk through setting up a throttle or fallback rule in the UI?
[04:00] Samir Patel: Sure - go to the route config panel: you can set SLOs (p95 latency), a cost threshold, and an automatic fallback that routes to a cheaper model or to a cached response. We'll demo a canary rollout too.
[04:14] Samir Patel: (clicks) Here's an existing route - note current p95 is 220ms, cost per 1k calls is $12. If we enable a quantized variant we estimate cost goes down to $8 with p95 rising to 260ms. You can run a canary at 10% traffic to validate quality.
[04:31] Ethan Ruiz: That delta is ok for some flows, not for the triage chat. We need sub-200ms for that one.
[04:36] Laura Gomez: Which is where Dedicated comes in?
[04:39] Maya Chen: Exactly. Dedicated capacity gives you predictable latency and throughput; you lose some of the cost-shifts from multi-tenant hosting but you get SLO-backed latency. You can still use the same console to monitor and route.
[04:51] Marco (PM): How do we estimate Dedicated sizing? We have peaks of 1k reqs/min with 75-token average output.
[04:58] Samir Patel: We'll follow up with a sizing doc; typically we ask for a representative traffic profile and run a short benchmark. For 1k reqs/min at 75 tokens, we'd suggest a small Dedicated pool, but we'll model batching behavior because effective throughput changes with batch windows.
[05:14] Priya Nair: For pilots, do you provide benchmark scripts or do we run them?
[05:18] Samir Patel: We provide both - a benchmark harness and can run a hosted benchmark for you. For Private, we can provide an on-prem benchmark guide.
[05:25] Laura Gomez: On the cost modeling spreadsheet, what inputs do you need?
[05:28] Maya Chen: Ideally: per-route RPS, average input/output tokens, model variant choices, SLA needs, and whether you want Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We'll populate cost-per-token and show sensitivity.
[05:40] Ethan Ruiz: Will that show quantization impact and cache hit-rate scenarios?
[05:44] Samir Patel: Yes - there's toggles for cache hit-rate (0-80%) and quantization savings. We include conservative and optimistic columns.
[05:52] Marco (PM): Any compliance red flags for our EU customer data?
[05:55] Priya Nair: (to Maya) We need data residency in EU and SOC2 Type II.
[05:59] Maya Chen: We support EU regions and have SOC2 docs - I'll share the pack after the call. For Private deployments we can point you to our on-prem or VPC options to keep things in-region.
[06:10] Laura Gomez: Perfect. One more thing on the console: can we export per-route bills to our finance system?
[06:15] Samir Patel: There's an export API and CSV export. Each line item includes route id, model, tokens, cost, and timestamp - you can ingest that into your billing system.
[06:24] Ethan Ruiz: Nice. Any limitations on retention of analytics data?
[06:27] Samir Patel: Hosted default retention is 90 days, with paid retention add-ons up to multi-year. For Private you control retention.
[06:34] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we go to next steps: We'll share SOC2 + data residency docs, Samir will send the cost-model workbook and a recommended Dedicated sizing draft, and Ethan will send a sample traffic profile. Pilot goal: 2-week throughput and canary test.
[06:48] Laura Gomez: Sounds good. What about pricing cadence - monthly vs annual?
[06:52] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based monthly. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commit options. We'll include pricing scenarios in the workbook.
[07:02] Priya Nair: Also want to confirm logging retention and log access controls - will look at the docs.
[07:06] Maya Chen: Absolutely.
[07:08] Marco (PM): Ok thanks all.
[07:10] Samir Patel: I'll drop the cost workbook in the thread, plus a short how-to for the console features we demoed.
[07:18] Laura Gomez: Appreciate it.
[07:20] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with timing for the pilot kickoff.
[07:23] Ethan Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[07:25] End of recording

Notes about transcript: occasional transcription errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache") are present; timestamps approximate. Links referenced during call: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (shared by Maya), cost workbook link (to be shared by Samir).
